note: Role of every variable of the twin's variable catalogue for the multivariate time-series work (forecasting and explanation). Roles are a design convention, not a model parameter. They exist to keep one rule: a covariate whose FUTURE values enter a forecast must be known at the cut-off (a weather forecast, a plan the user commits to); anything the twin computes after the cut-off is never a future covariate (no leakage). Every catalogue variable appears exactly once; the validation test fails otherwise.

roles.target: what a forecast predicts (and what an explanation explains)
roles.known_future_covariate: exogenous or planned: its future values are known at the cut-off
roles.decision_covariate: an actuator the user or a controller sets: a known future covariate only when the plan is given (what-if), a past-only covariate otherwise
roles.past_only_covariate: known up to the cut-off only
roles.context_only: enters the narrative, not the model (stage, accumulators, bookkeeping)
roles.excluded: not used as an input or a target (not represented by the twin, or a duplicate of another variable)

crop_stage.why: categorical phenological stage; selects the thresholds of crop_config.json

biomass_total_g_m2.why: accumulator; season KPI source, not an hourly driver

leaf_area_index.why: slow crop state that shapes transpiration and light interception

root_zone_water_mm.why: the same state as soil_water_vwc_m3_m3 in another unit

irrigation_mm.why: irrigation is a plan or a controller decision

precipitation_mm.why: rain reaching the crop: weather forecast outdoors, zero indoors

drainage_mm.why: consequence of irrigation and soil state

transpiration_mm.why: consequence of weather and crop state

evaporation_mm.why: consequence of weather and crop state

et0_mm.why: computed from the weather of the same step (and from the ET0 method chosen)

temperature_c.why: climate objective: the air the crop experiences

vpd_kpa.why: climate objective: drives transpiration and stress

radiation_w_m2.why: radiation reaching the crop depends on the shading actuator; the exogenous outdoor radiation is a separate forcing variable (see required_catalogue_additions)

water_stress.why: derived from the state by the twin's rules; derive it from a forecast with the same rules instead of forecasting it

growth_factor.why: explanatory bridge: the combined limiter of growth, shows which stress costs yield

co2_ppm.why: greenhouse CO2 (a decision when enrichment is planned: then decision_covariate in a what-if)

greenhouse_ventilation_fraction.why: resulting vent opening, which includes the built-in venting (not a plan)

greenhouse_shading_fraction.why: screen: a plan or a controller decision

control_electric_kw.why: consequence of the commands and the user's equipment

control_energy_kwh.why: consequence of the commands and the user's equipment

control_energy_kwh_cumulative.why: cumulative: forecast the rate, accumulate afterwards

required_catalogue_additions.note: The exogenous forcing the twin already uses (snapshot.outdoor_weather) is not yet a catalogue variable. Phase 6.1 adds these as FORCING variables so a frame can carry the known-future covariates.
